body:
## The defect

`.github/workflows/tests.yml`'s `Test Suite Summary` job gates every dependency
with the same shape:

    if [[ "${{ needs.fast-tests.result }}" == "failure" ]]; then exit 1; fi

`needs.<job>.result` is one of `success | failure | cancelled | skipped`. Testing
only for `failure` means **`cancelled` and `skipped` both pass**, and the job ends
with an unconditional `echo "✅ Test suite completed"`. Nothing anywhere asserts a
dependency actually succeeded.

Same pattern for `frontend-build`, `integration-tests` and `e2e-tests`.

## Live evidence

PR #1515, observed 2026-08-10:

    Fast Tests (Smoke + Unit):  CANCELLED
    Test Suite Summary:         SUCCESS      <-- required context, green

The tests never completed and the summary that exists to report on them says
they passed. The job carries `if: always()`, so a run cancelled by
`concurrency: cancel-in-progress` still produces a green summary attached to
that head SHA.

## Severity — real, but NOT merge-enabling today

`Fast Tests (Smoke + Unit)` is itself a required context in ruleset 15871246, so
a CANCELLED one blocks the merge on its own. The summary's false green does not
currently let anything through. What it does do is misreport to every human and
script that reads "Test Suite Summary: SUCCESS" as "the suite passed" — which is
the same absence-reads-as-success class as F-436d41, one level up.

## Why this was NOT fixed on the spot

The obvious fix — `!= "success"` — is not obviously safe, and this gate runs on
every PR:

- `fast-tests` and `frontend-build` have no `if:` and always run, so `!= "success"`
  is correct for those two.
- `integration-tests` and `e2e-tests` are legitimately skipped via the
  `IS_BUILD_PR` / `IS_FRONTEND_PR` path gates, so `!= "success"` would red every
  docs-only PR.
- With `if: always()`, a superseded run would then report FAILURE rather than a
  false SUCCESS. Failing closed is better than the current behaviour, but it puts
  spurious reds on PRs whose only sin was being pushed to twice.
- `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` avoids that by not reporting at all on a cancelled
  run — but a **skipped** required check can score as satisfied, which would trade
  this hole for a quieter one.

Each option needs a real run to confirm, and re-gating every PR's CI deserves that
rather than a plausible-looking one-liner. Proposed: `!= "success"` for the two
unconditional jobs, keep the applicability logic for the two conditional ones, and
verify a superseded-run case end to end before merging.
title: Test Suite Summary reports success when a required job was CANCELLED — it tests for failure, never for success
